newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lehman for switch to Porsche.
newsitem.headline: Lehman for switch to Porsche.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Lehman Brothers on Wednesday recommended a switch to shares in luxury carmaker Porsche AG from BMW and Volkswagen, as Porsche shares were now cheap and lagging the others.
Lehman said it was reiterating its "1 Buy" rating on Porsche, with a year-end price target of 3,000 marks, an upside of 48 percent.
"In the four months between November and early March, Porsche's stock price rose by 100 percent from 1,000 marks to 2,000 marks, outperforming the DAX by 65 percent."
"After such performance it is unsurprising that the market then ignored the stock, despite the increasingly spectacular equity story," Lehman Bros said in an analysis of the stock.

Porsche preference shares were amongst the top performers in bourse trade on Wednesday, up 130 marks, or 6.40 percent, at 1,160 marks in mid-session bourse, while the overall market was up 29.50 points, or 0.89 percent, at 3,357.18.
Lehman Brothers said the stock had become the "German automotive laggard", having underperformed VW by 20 percent and BMW by 15 percent in the six weeks since the beginning of March.

The stock had become cheap with its price/equity multiple on full year 1998/99 only 12.6 times, compared to 17.4 times at BMW. As such it was "time to buy again", Lehman Brothers said, adding: "And just look at the dollar...."
